title: Mistral raises €3B as Europe's AI champion courts China, Microsoft and Samsung
source_used: ActuIA (analysis of the round, 7 Oct 2026) and Brief IA (9 Oct 2026). The Dealroom page is blocked by Cloudflare (HTTP 403) and its note could not be read.
key_facts: ActuIA says Mistral AI announced on 8 September a €3 billion equity raise led by Samsung Electronics, taking its post-money valuation above €21 billion, up from about €11.7 billion in September 2025.
Samsung is committing up to €1 billion, according to Sifted, its largest publicly disclosed investment in a European AI lab.
Other participants named in reports of the announcement include Scaleup Europe, PSG Equity, Nvidia, ASML, BlackRock, Advent, Bpifrance, Salesforce and BNP Paribas.
Samsung makes memory, Nvidia the processors and ASML the chip-making machines Mistral's training depends on, so all three are now suppliers and shareholders.
ActuIA notes the €3 billion is an equity injection while the €21 billion valuation is negotiated between shareholders, not cash.
Brief IA says chief executive Arthur Mensch says the €3 billion will be entirely dedicated to buying computing capacity, and that Mistral launched Mistral Large 4 on 6 Oct 2026.
ActuIA says Mistral's first data centre, with Eclairion at Bruyeres-le-Chatel, is 44 megawatts and is to house about 13,800 Nvidia GB300 processors.
The Dealroom note dated 10 Oct 2026 adds that Mistral "courts China, Microsoft and Samsung" (headline only; content not read).
quote_evidence: Mistral AI announced on 8 September a €3 billion equity raise, led by Samsung Electronics, taking its post-money valuation to more than €21 billion, up from around €11.7 billion in the previous round in September 2025.
The €3 billion is an equity injection; the €21 billion valuation is negotiated between shareholders, not cash.
Arthur Mensch specifies that this amount will be entirely dedicated to acquiring additional computing capacity.
why_it_matters_hint: Samsung, Nvidia and ASML are now both suppliers and shareholders of Mistral, in a market limited by access to components; but the round itself dates from September.
notes: OLDER NEWS RE-DATED: the round was announced on 8 Sep 2026; the pool item is a 10 Oct Dealroom note on it (blocked, content unknown, so what is new in it is unverified). Read ActuIA and Brief IA instead; Traders Union (9 Oct) was also blocked (HTTP 403). Brief IA gives the spending plan as the chief executive's statement from a France Inter interview, not independently checked. Not in our archived editions of 27 Sep to 10 Oct.
